newsitem.title: FRANCE: Turnout rises in French parliamentary election.
newsitem.headline: Turnout rises in French parliamentary election.

text.p: Voter turnout in Sunday's runoff round of France's parliamentary election stood at 58.10 percent at 5 p.m. (1500 GMT), against 54.51 percent at the same time in the first round a week ago, the Interior Ministry said.
Among key factors in the election is the behaviour of the high proportion of electors -- 31.55 percent -- who stayed away from the polls in the first round.
In the last National Assembly election in 1993, turnout at the same time of day stood at 57.80.
The outcome of the election was thrown wide open after the Socialist-Communist bloc scored an upset win against the ruling centre-right coalition in the May 25 first round.

Polling stations opened at 8 a.m. (0600 GMT) in mainland France and were closing at 8 p.m. (1800 GMT), when first results projections will be released. The weather turned cloudy in most parts with showers in the south.

In the first round, when the combined left polled 40.1 percent of the vote to 36.5 for the centre-right, the gap between key candidates in 80 of the 577 constituencies was less than two percentage points.
